rationale: Because clean-surplus accounting makes (ni − Δceq) essentially net payout (dividends + repurchases − issuance, contaminated by OCI), this is a near-mechanical restatement of the archive's already-tested "Gross Profit Net Payout Bottleneck" (profitability IND_RANK ∧ net-payout RANK) and also overlaps the published net-payout/composite-issuance anomalies.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's "Post Interest Net Deleverager" and the inverse of "Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict" — cash profitability bottlenecked with falling liability intensity — with Δ(lt/at) highly collinear with Δ(debt/at) and largely subsumed by the known asset-growth/NOA-change anomalies.

Conditioning equity issuance on the firm's own time-series profitability peak is a defensible market-timing refinement that is internally consistent with the negative sign and distinct from the archive's accrual-based issuer conditioning, though it remains a variant of the well-documented share-issuance anomaly with sstk-driven low coverage and a noisy long leg under the MIN construction.

The debt-financed-dividend-with-fading-margins story is economically coherent and sign-consistent, but the triple nested MIN plus a 5-period trend and dvc requirement will compress cross-sectional variation and coverage, so the main risk is a statistically fragile, composition-unstable spread rather than a conceptual flaw.

This is essentially the sign-flipped mirror of the archive's "Post Interest Net Deleverager" with Δ(xint/at) mechanically collinear with Δ(debt/at), and the MIN puts a known positive predictor (high profitability) inside the short leg, so the two components fight each other rather than reinforcing the hypothesis.

Self-admittedly a refinement of the failed gen-0 "Margin Up Debt Down" (indicator replaced by rank, plus an issuance leg already explored in "Cash Profit Capital Raise Conflict"), which makes it a cosmetic rather than substantive change to a mechanism the archive has already found weak.
